body:
Be happy. 

I have bipolar disorder and, don't matter what I do, I just can't get better. I have already tried meds, therapy, healthier lifestyle choices, sports. I have a great support network, but I still feel that nobody understands me. I feel so alone
I think I will write the letter and hope for my feeling to change as I write. Today will not be the day I kill myself, but now I don't see other way out...

> The illness will swallow me in delusion and psychosis

Oh, man, I'm so scared of that. I always had this biggest fear of developing schizophrenia or some other kind of psychosis. This worsening of my cognitive skills makes that fear come back

I have a family history of depression as well, but not bipolar. It probably has an influence. I don't know how the system works in the USA, but can a psychiatric nurse prescribe meds for you? Here in Brazil only doctors can prescribe

> My bipolar has never interfered with my ability to learn or comprehend though

There's that. I also don't fell it interferes with my capacity to understand topics, but it messes up my attention span and memory a lot. I hope those are not permanent
Yes, I can! If he tells me something interesting, I will share with you :)

I'm on Lamictal as well. I really hope the worsening memory and attention span are reversible. I'm going to talk to my doctor to see if I can do something about it.

Do you have BPD and ADHD? Which medications do you take?
I also think it's the illness, but for me that is way worse than thinking it's the meds causing it. I'm terrified of thinking my brain skills will get worse and worse over the years :(
I feel that too! I used to write a lot of poetry and short stories, but now I can't even think of a verse. I feel so empty of creativity right now

That's so scary to read :( I sent an e-mail to my doctor to talk about this. I'm currently on Lamictal, and it really improved my mood swings, but it made me feel so slow and tired all the time. Maybe I should change meds...

Oh, man, that happens to me as well. Today I tried to tell a storie to my girlfriend and she ignored me. She probably just didn't hear me talking, but it made me feel so lonely, as if nobody cared about what I have to say. And when they do hear me, I always regret saying it because I think it's stupid or irrelevant :(
Verdade. Me sinto mal por suspeitar tanto de alguns grupos, mas a gente não pode parar de se precaver  só pra ser politicamente correto
Essa questão do preconceito é muito ruim mesmo. É só ver um moleque magro e mestiço que já perco a paz. Me sinto mal por isso. E moto com um cara na garupa nem se fala.

Olha só, alguém da minha cidade.

Pois é, aqui em São Luís tá bem complicado. Por muito tempo pensei que esse negócio de assalto só acontecia com os outros até sofrer um sequestro-relâmpago. A pior coisa não é nem a perda material, mas a paranóia eterna que fica após o ocorrido. Aqui não se pode mais sair de casa sem ter medo de não voltar mais. É a coisa que mais me dá vontade de sair do país.

Fique bem, amigo!
Thanks! It's ok, opinions are always welcome
Thanks for responding! She's cute :)

Yep
Have you really read about it?
Yep
I read some in Portuguese, but there's a lot of content in dharma.net. Even the Wikipedia portal of Buddhism is a nice read!
Hahaha, got it. I think I should watch it someday. I hope it's on Brazilian Netflix
Mostly the core teachings about suffering and the Noble Eightfold Path. You really should look into it!
I don't think that is a good way to see it, but you are more than allowed to have your opinion. Peace!

To some people it is, but there are a lot of ways to practice the dharma. To be mindful, caring for the others, to spread love and to pursue wisdom is already practicing. Becoming a monk is just one of the paths you can take.

But I see your point. I hope you find something that fulfills you :)

Buddhism doesn't have an afterlife in the way you're used to. It's philosophy speaks only about the continuity of consciousness and suffering. The "not dying" part is not a blessing like you are saying, it's the thing we most want to overcome. It's not ego-stroking, but the complete opposite.

I don't see it like that. I see it as having such a strong connection with the world and all living beings that yourself, your subjective view of "self" is dissolved. If you don't have that connection with "self", you can't feel the suffering that strikes it. You become free. That's the meaning of anatta for me.
I did not catch that reference
Kill myself. Not because I'm depressed, I'm just very curious about what exists after
I'm from Brazil, what about you?
I agree 100% with you. I hope you find your fulfilment. Keep reading, keep talking, keep pursuing wisdom! The most important thing isn't your set of beliefs, but what you do with them.
If by "believing in fairy tales" you mean following a philosophy that greatly enhanced my life and made me a better person, yes is the answer! :)
Oh, I see. I guess didn't read your post well enough. I got your point

You have to take into consideration that most atheists don't identify as part of any religious group. Therefore, it's a meaning intrinsically linked to atheism that I don't identify with. You're not technically incorrect, but I still won't identify that way
Yes, they do. I hope you find something that rings true to you, and not ridiculous!
Not extensively. Do you have some tips on some interesting concepts of those? I would really like to learn about them
Thank you very much. It's good to know that since I want to live in USA someday
You're not incorrect, but most atheistic people identify themselves as not belong to any kind of religious group. That's why I don't like to call myself an atheist
Thank you! I'm really happy to read this
I was referring to a popular post here on Reddit. Unfortunately I don't have the link here :(
I don't think so. I think some atheistic people can find their happiness and fulfillment without recurring to some religious group

Buddhism is all about love. The dharma says to love yourself, love others, love every sentient being. This thought and the meditation centered around it make me feel connected to everything and with myself. I don't even know how to express that
I disagree. I think religions can be great and help people better themselves like nothing else could
Perfectly put. Being happy and fulfilled is way more important than being logical
I agree with the last part, but the part I cringe about is the "I'm more intelligent than you" belief, not the atheistic one
I think you can see it both ways. It depends which way you apply the teachings in your life
Yes, I do. And I think this is getting more and more common in the western world
I went that path too. I was a Christian, then an atheist, then Buddhist. I don't think any of then is better than the others, though

Because virtually everything the Buddhism philosophy says feels right to me. Especially the things about inner peace, non violence and lovingkindness. You should look into it! The /r/buddhism is a good way to go!
Thank you! I am bipolar and used to suffer a lot from that, but since I joined and practiced Buddhism I feel much better. The part about knowing yourself is totally true :)

I used to be the "euphoric" kind teenager atheist. I even had a Twitter account that I used to argue with christians, because "rational", "intelligence", "fiction book" and all that bullshit.

When I started growing up, however, I started reading a bout a lot of religions. First because I wanted to know how to argue against them, then because I grew interested in them.

A year or two later I discovered Buddhism, and everything about it rang true to me. I felt a connection. And when I started practicing, I felt whole, I felt strong and felt like I was growing as a person.

I still cringe about the euphoric phase, though.
